members.name: multi_timeframe_breakout_v1
members.thesis: A breakout that is confirmed on both the 1-min AND 5-min timeframes has significantly higher reliability than a breakout on either timeframe alone. The 5-min chart filters out noise that causes false breakouts on the 1-min chart, while the 1-min chart provides precise entry timing within the broader
entry_long: 5min_close > DC_upper_5m (5-min breakout confirmed on current or last completed 5-min bar)
members.exit_target: 0.6% from entry (multi-timeframe breakouts tend to produce larger moves)
filters: no entries before 10:00 (5-min lookback of 30 = 150 min, so need ~2.5 hours; starts mid-morning from prior day close calc) or after 14:00
weaknesses: Dual-timeframe confirmation is very strict — many valid breakouts on one timeframe will not be confirmed on the other
The 5-min lookback of 30 bars = 150 minutes; intraday session is only 375 minutes, so data is limited early in the day
Operational complexity: need to maintain 1-min and 5-min bar feeds simultaneously with aligned timestamps

members.name: multi_timeframe_confirmation_v1
members.thesis: Using 1-min bars for entry but requiring confirmation from a 5-min or 15-min signal reduces noise dramatically. When a 5-min EMA crossover fires (EMA_9 > EMA_21 on 5-min bars) AND the 1-min RSI(7) is oversold (< 25), you're entering a 5-min trend on a 1-min pullback. The higher timeframe confirms di
filters: no trades first 15 min or last 30 min
5-min trend determines direction; 1-min is entry only
weaknesses: 5-min trend can lag — by the time EMA crossover fires on 5-min, the 1-min move may be mostly done
RSI(7) < 25 on 1-min during a 5-min uptrend is an aggressive pullback — might be the start of a reversal, not a pullback
Maintaining two timeframe calculations adds implementation complexity
